newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran denies harbouring Saudi suspect - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies harbouring Saudi suspect - newspaper.

text.p: An Iranian official in remarks published on Monday denied a U.S. newspaper report that Iran was harbouring the alleged mastermind of a bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia last year.

The London-based Al-Hayat Arabic language newspaper quoted Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi as denying that Ahmad Ibrahim Ahmad Mughassil "was living as a guest of and under the protection of the Iranian government".
"This accusation is unfounded and has no truth to it and we have said before and we reaffirm that we have no links of any kind to the perpetrators of the bombing operation," he said.

The American tabloid Newsday on Saturday quoted a U.S. counterterrorism specialist familiar with the bombing investigation as saying that Mughassil was believed to be living under the protection of the Iranian government.
A court document filed in Canada on Thursday identified Mughassil as the mastermind of the truck bombing.
The Canadian document came to light during a deportation hearing against another suspect in the bombing, Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh, who is being held in Canada.
Newsday said the fact the Saudi bomb-plot suspect had been given safe haven by the Iranians gave credence to growing evidence that Iran played a major role in the attack.
Mohammadi accused the United States of trying to implicate Iran in the bombing in order to alleviate international and Arab pressure on Israel.
"It appears that Washington wants to lessen the impact of popular and political pressure on the Zionist government...for the continuation of its agressive expansionist policies," he said.
Mohammadi was referring to Israel's recent decision to build a new housing project in Arab East Jerusalem.
The newspaper also said American and Canadian intelligence officials believed Syria gave tacit approval to the June 25 bombing near Dhahran.
